description: Vanilla/Paper Minecraft Java Edition server, logs/latest.log: [10:15:31] [Server thread/INFO]: message. The bracketed field before the slash is the JVM thread, not a logger in the Serilog sense, but it plays the same role — 'Server thread' for normal ticks, 'Server thread/Async Chat Thread' etc for plugin work — so it is kept as log.logger.

grok.description: MSGBODY, not GREEDYDATA — a crash's stack trace is joined into one multiline event before it reaches this pipeline, and GREEDYDATA stops at the first newline while grok anchors $ per line, so a plain %{GREEDYDATA:_tmp.msg}$ would match only the exception's first line and silently throw the trace away when 'set message copy_from _tmp.msg' runs below.

script.description: logs/latest.log carries a clock time but no date — the day is only implicit in the filename it rolls into at midnight (logs/2026-09-25-1.log.gz). Elastic Agent tails the file live, so ingest time is a good stand-in for the missing date: take today's date in the server's local timezone and graft the log line's own H:m:s onto it. If that produces a time more than a minute in the future, the line was written just before local midnight and read just after, so roll back a day. A line delayed by more than a minute in the harvester's read queue — the agent down, a burst on restart replaying a backlog — still gets today's date instead of the day it actually happened; nothing here can tell those two cases apart from the clock time alone.
script.source: def tz = ZoneId.of(ctx.event?.timezone != null ? ctx.event.timezone : 'UTC'); def now = Instant.parse(ctx._tmp.now).atZone(tz); def p = ctx._tmp.time.splitOnToken(':'); def dt = now.withHour(Integer.parseInt(p[0])).withMinute(Integer.parseInt(p[1])).withSecond(Integer.parseInt(p[2])).withNano(0); if (dt.isAfter(now.plusMinutes(1))) { dt = dt.minusDays(1); } ctx['@timestamp'] = DateTimeFormatter.ISO_INSTANT.format(dt.toInstant());
